questions.stem: Aplicando «Interpret a proverb in a log note / Match the proverb to its meaning. / Proverbs» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: None, because proverbs are opinions
options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

options.text: Más vale tarde que nunca, because it accepts lateness
No hay mal que por bien no venga, because it turns adversity into benefit
A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda, because it rewards early rising

questions.explanation: No hay mal que por bien no venga means something good can come from something bad. The other proverbs address lateness or early rising, not adversity turning into benefit.
questions.hint: Match the proverb to its meaning.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Identify a concluding sentence in a log

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «The last sentence, because it closes the argument.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Identify a concluding sentence in a log / Find the sentence that closes the argument. / Topic and concluding sentences». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.text: The first sentence, because it introduces the topic
No sentence, because the paragraph is open-ended
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "No sentence, because the paragraph is open-ended" for the governing rule

options.text: A middle sentence, because it gives detail
The last sentence, because it closes the argument

questions.explanation: The concluding sentence closes the argument and usually appears last. The paragraph's structure supports the last sentence as concluding. Option A ("The first sentence, because it introduces the topic") is wrong: confuses introduction with conclusion; Option C ("A middle sentence, because it gives detail") is wrong: confuses detail with conclusion; Option B ("No sentence, because the paragraph is open-ended") is wrong: mistakes a surface feature of "No sentence, because the paragraph is open-ended" for the governing rule.
questions.hint: Find the sentence that closes the argument.

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Además, because it signals an addition.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Con la pista «Use a connective in a log composition / Ask what logical relation the connective expresses. / Connectives in composition», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.text: Además, because it signals an addition
Sin embargo, because it signals a contrast
Por lo tanto, because it signals a consequence
Pero, because it signals opposition

questions.explanation: Además introduces an addition to the previous information. Sin embargo signals contrast, por lo tanto signals consequence, and pero signals opposition. Only además adds information.
questions.hint: Ask what logical relation the connective expresses.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cultural claim in a log

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «The claim overgeneralizes a practice to all Spaniards and asserts a fixed frequency.» « All Spaniards eat paella every Sunday » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Evaluate a cultural claim in a log / Check whether the claim is too broad to verify. / Checkable cultural claims» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

answer.exemplar: The claim overgeneralizes a practice to all Spaniards and asserts a fixed frequency. It cannot be verified because it is too broad and absolute. A checkable claim would be narrower and evidence-based, such as paella originating in Valencia.

questions.explanation: The claim is an overgeneralization that cannot be verified. It asserts a universal practice with a fixed frequency. Narrower, evidence-based claims are checkable.
questions.hint: Check whether the claim is too broad to verify.

questions.learningObjective: Preserve register when translating a log entry

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Se le informa que el tren se retrasa, formal construction.» « Te aviso que el tren se retrasa » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Preserve register when translating a log entry / Keep the formal register and the recipient. / Translating and preserving register». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.text: Se retrasa el tren, passive without recipient
Se le informa que el tren se retrasa, formal construction
El tren se retrasa, bare statement
Te aviso que el tren se retrasa, informal construction

questions.explanation: Se le informa que el tren se retrasa preserves the formal register of the original. Te aviso is informal. other options lose politeness or the recipient. Register must match the original. Option A ("Se retrasa el tren, passive without recipient") is wrong: omits the recipient; Option D ("Te aviso que el tren se retrasa, informal construction") is wrong: drops the formal register; Option C ("El tren se retrasa, bare statement") is wrong: loses politeness and recipient.
questions.hint: Keep the formal register and the recipient.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Recognize a drifted cognate in a log entry

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «éxito, because it means success not exit.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Recognize a drifted cognate in a log entry / Find the word whose meaning shifted. / Cognates that have drifted» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: salida, because it means exit
options.misconception: confuses the true equivalent with the drifted cognate

options.text: éxito, because it means success not exit
salir, because it means to leave
options.misconception: confuses a verb with the cognate

options.text: excusa, because it means excuse
options.misconception: confuses an unrelated word with the cognate

questions.explanation: Éxito is a cognate of English exit but means success in Spanish, showing drift. Salida is the true equivalent for exit. Option A ("salida, because it means exit") is wrong: confuses the true equivalent with the drifted cognate; Option C ("salir, because it means to leave") is wrong: confuses a verb with the cognate; Option D ("excusa, because it means excuse") is wrong: confuses an unrelated word with the cognate.
questions.hint: Find the word whose meaning shifted.
